title: Pro-etale open restriction data
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ and $h:W\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $X_W=X\times_YW$ with projections $g:X_W\to X$ and $f_W:X_W\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on the small pro-etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the canonical inverse-image adjunctions [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Define $R_X=f^{-1}R$, $R_W=h^{-1}R$, $R_{X_W}=g^{-1}R_X$, and $\operatorname{CoeffCmp}(f,h,R)=\operatorname{Iso}(f_W^{-1}R_W,R_{X_W})$. The canonical element $c$ of this type is the inverse of the component at $R$ of the inverse-image square comparison $g^{-1}f^{-1}\simeq f_W^{-1}h^{-1}$, obtained by adjoint conjugation from the projection-preserving base-change associativity isomorphism of site functors.

Use the categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the ordinary module pullback and direct image with their canonical adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $\operatorname{ModX}(f,R)=\operatorname{Mod}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R_X)$. When $h$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], define functors $\operatorname{Left}=h^{-1}f_*$ and $\operatorname{Right}=f_{W,*}g^{-1}$ from this category to $\operatorname{Mod}(W_{\mathrm{proet}},R_W)$; the coefficient identifications are identities except for $c$ on the $f_W$ edge.

For a weakly etale map $k:A\to B$, let $\operatorname{objectComposition}(k)$ send $(E\to A)$ to $(E\to A\to B)$. For a ring sheaf $S$ on $B$, an $S$-module $M$, and $E\in A_{\mathrm{proet}}$, define the canonical coprojection $\kappa_{k,S,M,E}:M(E\to B)\to(k^{-1}M)(E\to A)$ by evaluating the module adjunction unit on $E\to B$ and then restricting along the unit $E\to E\times_B A$ of site base change. For $E\in W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ define the section arrow $a_E:(E\times_W X_W\to X)\to(E\times_YX\to X)$ by the identity on $E$ and the projection $g$ on $X_W$.

For an isomorphism $\beta:\operatorname{Left}\simeq\operatorname{Right}$, define $\operatorname{Sectionwise}(f,h,R,\beta)$ to be the conjunction of: all coprojections $\kappa_{h,R,M,E}$ are bijective; all coprojections $\kappa_{g,R_X,N,F}$ are bijective; and, for every $R_X$-module $N$, every $E\in W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $s\in N(E\times_YX)$,
$$\beta_{N,E}\bigl(\kappa_{h,R,f_*N,E}(s)\bigr)=\kappa_{g,R_X,N,E\times_WX_W}\bigl(N(a_E)(s)\bigr).$$
The bijectivity assertions belong to the defined predicate; this definition does not assert that any $\beta$ satisfies it.
